setting.school_description: Japan's most prestigious hero-track school, tucked into the quiet residential blocks of Nerima Ward on Tokyo's western edge. Known nationwide for producing top Pro Heroes. Entry is brutally competitive — the entrance exam is genuinely dangerous, and only the top performers earn a spot. Class 1-A is the flagship hero course cohort, the class everyone outside watches and resents a little.

school_features.grounds: A walled campus that looks small from the street and isn't — training grounds, Battle Centres simulating real urban environments, dormitories (Heights Alliance), support labs, and classrooms built around quirk-integrated learning.
school_features.heights_alliance: The student dormitories. Each student has their own room but shares common spaces — kitchen, living room, laundry. Most of the campaign's downtime drama happens here.
school_features.battle_centres: Numbered training areas (I through VII) with different environments: city block, forest, industrial yard, interior combat. Used for both formal training and exams.
school_features.recommendations_and_rankings: Students are ranked internally. This matters more than it probably should to several members of Class 1-A.

city.name: Tokyo
city.description: The real city, mostly — busy, dense, and completely used to heroes by now. Hero sightings are a daily occurrence, agency branding is stitched into half the storefronts in Shibuya, and civilians have strong, loud opinions about the Pro Hero rankings. The wards the class actually spends time in each have their own texture.

districts.shibuya: Downtown commercial core. Agency-sponsored storefronts, the crossing's big public screens running hero ranking updates between ads. Where the class goes on free weekends.
districts.marunouchi: Glass-and-steel business district where the highest-ranked agencies keep their towers. Looks like money. Feels like a lobby.
districts.setagaya: Residential sprawl — quiet streets, parks, schools, families. Where most of the class's rescue-and-patrol work happens. Nothing here is glamorous and that's the point.
districts.kurogane_wharf: A working waterfront pocket on the Koto side of Tokyo Bay — old fish-market blocks, container yards, warehouses that changed hands too many times for anyone to track. Officially still part of the city's shipping backbone. Unofficially, it's Ruin's home turf, and has been for years.

hero_society.tone: Mostly functioning and genuinely exciting. Being a hero is cool. Hero rankings are watched like sports. U.A. students are minor celebrities at public events. The world feels alive and worth protecting.
hero_society.licensing: Heroes must hold a Hero License to engage in combat. Students operate under provisional licenses before graduating. Unlicensed quirk use in combat is technically criminal, which creates tension during patrol and internship arcs.
hero_society.pro_hero_culture: Pro heroes have sponsors, fan rankings, social media followings. Some are genuine legends. Some are PR machines. The class will meet both kinds.
hero_society.background_rot: Everyone in Tokyo knows the name Ruin. It's been running out of Kurogane Wharf for years — extortion, quirk-for-hire jobs, black-market support gear, a quiet quirk-research operation hiding behind a tech-consultancy shell. One villain group, six named members, no departments. The Hero Commission's dossier on Ruin is thick, but what it doesn't have is a face for the top of it. Everyone who's ever named a leader has used the same word — Undertow — and nobody official will confirm he exists. Separately, a real anti-licensing movement called Fracture has been getting louder at protests across the city; nobody — not the Commission, not Fracture's own leadership — has connected it to Ruin's money yet. Ruin isn't a mystery. Undertow is.

student_life.tone: The backbone of the campaign between dramatic arcs. Cooking arguments, study chaos, dorm drama, class rivalries, gossip about who likes who, culture festival disasters, sports festival tensions. This is as important as the combat.
quirks_of_daily_life: Toshida Shogoro's speech bubble head makes doorways a recurring hazard
Takazuki Hanori being invisible means people regularly sit on her or walk through her stuff
Nakaya Emari has accidentally short-circuited several pieces of common room electronics and refuses to apologise
Masahata Shikoji maintains a printed personal ranking chart on the common room fridge that everyone else ignores
Kinosho Kochimiko has the best strategic mind in the class and uses it exclusively to find the optimal napping location

class_dynamics.rivalries: Ando Iorai and Toragi Kayo both think they're the most dangerous person in the room. They are not. The most dangerous person in the room is usually Chozen Tadachi, who is currently staring at a wall.
class_dynamics.friendships: Kibi Kankei and Isokono Yoromu have an unspoken alliance based on being the most laid-back people in a class full of very intense personalities. Yoshibara Hiyoko's chaotic energy pairs oddly well with Nomi Igisa's quietness — they are somehow best friends.
class_dynamics.class_chaos_index: High. There are twenty people with unusual abilities living together. Something is always happening.

level_tiers.tier_1: Levels 1-3: First year begins. U.A. campus. Training, dorm life, first real danger.
level_tiers.tier_2: Levels 4-6: Sports Festival, Internships, Tokyo patrol. Getting serious.
level_tiers.tier_3: Levels 7-13: Ruin makes it personal. Culture Festival. Betrayal arc.
